title: Understand the project and write a clear contract
ability: Set up the workspace, understand the existing application, and turn a vague request into exact behaviour that can be tested.
gitverse: One personal semester repository, one GitVerse issue, and branch stage/01-discovery.
agent: GigaCode reads the existing files and explains the project. You verify its claims and do not let it change the application code yet.
artifact: A GitVerse issue with exact inputs and expected outputs for Stage 02, a checked work report, and no application-code changes.
goal: Set up your workspace, understand the starting application, and turn a vague feature request into exact behaviour that can be tested.
steps: Open your personal GitVerse repository, clone it, and open the project root in VS Code.
Run `npm test`, then `npm run start`. Open the address from the terminal and confirm that 12 tickets are visible.
Ask GigaCode to explain `src/data.js`, `src/tickets.js`, and `src/app.js`. Pick three claims from its answer and verify each one against the actual file.
Read `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md` and explain which rules Stage 02 must preserve.
Create a GitVerse issue named `Search, filters and sorting` using the provided issue template.
Write the exact Stage 02 contract in the issue: status filter, priority filter, case-insensitive search across title/location, and title sorting.
Run `git diff --exit-code -- index.html src tests styles.css` and save the result in `REPORT.md`. Application code must still be unchanged.
success: the application shows 12 tickets and the browser console has no errors
`REPORT.md` contains three GigaCode claims and the file/function used to verify each one
the GitVerse issue contains all five concrete examples from Step 7
the issue states what is out of scope: no API, database, authentication, or new dependency in Stage 02
`git diff --exit-code -- index.html src tests styles.css` returns exit code 0.
failure: the report only says “GigaCode explained the project” without checking its claims
the issue says “search should work correctly” without concrete examples
application code was already changed on this stage
the only evidence is a screenshot or an AI message saying everything is correct.
acceptance: the project runs and 5 tests pass
three AI claims are checked against real files
the issue contains exact input → expected output examples
defense: What is the difference between a statement from GigaCode, a file change in your working tree, and a Git commit? Which one of them proves that the program behaves correctly?

context.title: Starting point
context.body:
Campus ServiceDesk already shows 12 sample support tickets. There is no search, filtering, sorting, API, or database yet.

Your goal today is **not** to implement the next feature. First understand the project and define exactly what Stage 02 must do.
